items.title: Amodei hands the Security Council a step-by-step governance playbook
items.summary: Policy: Calling AI 'the most important global security issue facing the world today,' Amodei proposed simple broad-consensus treaties like a ban on AI bioweapon development, global evaluation and verification systems so states can check rival labs' commitments, global testing standards for loss-of-control and misuse, and a global notification system. The poles are set: Anthropic on one end, the White House on the other, OpenAI in the middle.

items.title: Multiplayer AI is the biggest design problem nobody agrees on
items.summary: Enterprise: Ethan Mollick calls multiplayer AI one of the biggest non-technical problems in AI right now, with approaches stuck at 'AI as a person in your group chat.' Open questions abound: who is the principal — the user, with the agent as proxy, or the agent itself with its own identity and memory? And the hardest part may not be technical at all: getting a whole team to adopt one shared way of working is more org design than engineering.

items.title: We've repeatedly seen a pattern where AI performance in new intellectual domains goes from weak to superhuman in a matter of a few years.
items.summary: Models: — Dario Amodei, promoting the Claude discovery on X. Amodei's math timeline: high-school-level in 2023, competition-level in 2024, minor open problems in 2025, and the top open problems in mathematics by late 2026. He believes AI for biology is on the same exponential — the wet lab exists to physically confirm results, and the goal remains 'cure most diseases in five to ten years.'

items.title: Beware the sub-agent burn: frontier models all the way down
items.summary: Models: Fable 5.1's current default uses the most advanced model not just as coordinator but for every sub-agent it spins up. Many users have handed it a standard task and come back to find five or ten frontier-model sub-agents have torched a major chunk of the usage cap on research that didn't need them. Knowing where different model tiers belong is becoming a core discipline.

items.title: When it comes to LLMs, personality is UX
items.summary: ◆ The Take: Even ruthless early adopters who profess to only care about performance have personality preferences — the Opus excitement is about the pleasure of use, not new capabilities.
